teaser.en: At Kibuyuni, women who were traditionally kept from fishing now farm the sea, and turn their seaweed into soap, lotion and juice.
teaser.sw: Huko Kibuyuni, wanawake ambao kwa desturi walizuiwa kuvua samaki sasa hulima bahari, na hugeuza mwani wao kuwa sabuni, losheni na sharubati.

summary.en: Spinosum is a spiny red-brown seaweed farmed in the shallow lagoons of the south coast, mostly by women. Dried and sold for carrageenan, or made into soaps and lotions, it has become an important source of income at Kibuyuni near Shimoni.
summary.sw: *Spinosum* ni mwani wenye miba wa rangi ya kahawia-nyekundu unaolimwa katika mahori yasiyo na kina ya pwani ya kusini, hasa na wanawake. Ukikaushwa na kuuzwa kwa ajili ya *carrageenan*, au ukitengenezwa sabuni na losheni, umekuwa chanzo muhimu cha kipato huko Kibuyuni karibu na Shimoni.

about.en: Spinosum is a red alga, not a true plant, with branching stems that are red-brown and covered in short spines. It grows quickly from small cuttings, and a farmer can harvest it about every six weeks. It is rich in carrageenan, a natural gel used to thicken foods and cosmetics.
about.sw: *Spinosum* ni mwani mwekundu, si mmea halisi, wenye mashina yenye matawi ya rangi ya kahawia-nyekundu yaliyofunikwa na miba mifupi. Hukua haraka kutoka kwenye vipandikizi vidogo, na mkulima anaweza kuuvuna takriban kila wiki sita. Una *carrageenan* nyingi, jeli ya asili inayotumika kuongeza uzito wa vyakula na vipodozi.

where.en: It is farmed on off-bottom lines and stakes in the shallow lagoons at Kibuyuni near Shimoni and in other south-coast villages. The Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute (KMFRI) has run a model farm there since 2012. At low tide, the rows of stakes and ropes are easy to see from the shore.
where.sw: Hulimwa kwenye kamba na vigingi vilivyoinuliwa juu ya sakafu katika mahori yasiyo na kina huko Kibuyuni karibu na Shimoni na katika vijiji vingine vya pwani ya kusini. Taasisi ya Utafiti wa Bahari na Uvuvi ya Kenya (KMFRI) imeendesha shamba la mfano huko tangu 2012. Wakati wa maji kupwa, safu za vigingi na kamba huonekana kwa urahisi kutoka ufuoni.

uses.en:
Farmers tie cuttings to ropes stretched between stakes in the shallows, then harvest the seaweed about six weeks later, dry it and sell it as a source of carrageenan.

The women of Kibuyuni also add value to their harvest themselves, making soap, body lotion, shampoo, juice and hair food from it.
uses.sw:
Wakulima hufunga vipandikizi kwenye kamba zilizonyooshwa kati ya vigingi katika maji yasiyo na kina, kisha huvuna mwani takriban wiki sita baadaye, huukausha na kuuuza kama chanzo cha *carrageenan*.

Wanawake wa Kibuyuni pia huongeza thamani ya mavuno yao wenyewe, wakitengeneza sabuni, losheni ya mwili, shampuu, sharubati na mafuta ya nywele kutokana nao.

culture.en: Seaweed farming on the south coast is mostly women's work: about three in four farmers are women, who traditionally could not fish. It has given them their own income from the sea. The Kibuyuni farmers' group became a cooperative in 2019.
culture.sw: Kilimo cha mwani katika pwani ya kusini ni kazi ya wanawake zaidi: takriban wakulima watatu kati ya wanne ni wanawake, ambao kwa desturi hawakuweza kuvua samaki. Kimewapa kipato chao wenyewe kutoka baharini. Kikundi cha wakulima wa Kibuyuni kiligeuka kuwa chama cha ushirika mwaka 2019.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. In Swahili, farmed seaweed is *mwani*. In English it is spinosum seaweed, and its scientific name is *Eucheuma denticulatum*.
names.sw: Bado halijarekodiwa jina la Kidigo. Kwa Kiswahili, mwani unaolimwa huitwa *mwani*. Kwa Kiingereza unaitwa *spinosum seaweed*, na jina lake la kisayansi ni *Eucheuma denticulatum*.

conservation.en: It is a farmed crop. Harvests suffer in warm-water die-offs and from 'ice-ice' disease, which bleaches and kills the seaweed.
conservation.sw: Ni zao la shambani. Mavuno huathirika wakati wa vifo vingi vinavyosababishwa na maji ya joto na kutokana na ugonjwa wa 'ice-ice', unaoufifisha rangi mwani na kuuua.
